previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with malaise, body aches, tremors, and urinary symptoms including dysuria and hesitancy. She had a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, gastroparesis, and recent hip fracture. Evaluation revealed pyuria suggestive of a complicated urinary tract infection, despite negative cultures. She was treated with ciprofloxacin and showed clinical improvement. Mild confusion on admission resolved, attributed to infection and possible deliriogenic medications. Her nortriptyline was reduced, and thyroid function tests indicated a need for levothyroxine dose review. She remained stable, completed treatment, and was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics and follow up with her primary care provider.

ACTIVE ISSUES
-------------

# Syncope
# Hypoglycemia
# Type I DM
The patient presented after having been found down at home by 
her husband with frothing at her mouth after having lost 
consciousness. Most likely in the setting of hypoglycemia given 
initial FSBG of 30 and response to glucose. She has history of 
orthostatic hypotension but has been gaining weight recently and 
appeared volume up on exam, making hypovolemia less likely. Lack 
of palpitations and chest pain, as well as exertional symptoms 
make primary cardiac etiology less likely. CT head negative for 
acute abnormality. ___ was consulted to assist with glycemic 
control and recommended adjustement of her insulin regimen. No 
recurrent loss of consciousness during hospital stay. No acute 
events on telemetry. Discharge insulin regimen: lantus 10u qpm, 
70/30 8u before peritoneal dialysis (to be adjusted based on how 
many cycles of dialysis she completes), and an insulin sliding 
scale. 

# Hyponatremia
Likely secondary to hypervolemia in the setting of renal 
dysfunction and insufficient dialysis for past week prior to 
presentation. Serum osmolality was high-normal, likely given 
elevated BUN and glucose. Stable during hospital stay. 
Discharge sodium: 126

# ESRD on PD:
# Hypervolemia:
Hypervolemic on admission, c/b hyponatremia as above. Neprhology 
was consulted to assiste with dialysis and fluid management. 
Patient was continued on daily peritoneal dialysis without 
complications. Discharge weight: 72.8 kg (160.49 lb) 

# Severe gastroparesis:
Patient presented with nausea and vomiting, most likely in the 
setting of a gastroparesis flare. Of note, she stated that her 
symptoms on admission were within the range of her baseline 
symptoms of her gastroparesis. She was continued on Zofran with 
intermittent symptom control with Ativan. Stable on discharge. 

# Upper respiratory infection:
Patient started to experience URI symptoms one week prior to 
presentation. Most likely in the setting of a viral infection 
vs. volume overload. Low suspicion for bacterial infection / 
pneumonia given absence of fever and leukocytosis, unremarkable 
pulmonary exam, and clear chest X-ray. Symptoms resolved during 
admission with supportive management.

-------------------
CHRONIC ISSUES
-------------------

# Orthostatic hypotension:
Chronic. On midodrine and hydrocortisone at home. Low suspicion 
for contribution to current presentation for syncope given 
hypervolemia on exam. Continued home midodrine.

# Chronic pain
# Fibromyalgia
# Chronic fatigue
# Peripheral neuropathy
Stable. Continued home dilaudid, pregabalin, modafinil, 
tizanidine, and Nortriptyline 10mg daily.

# Hypothyroidism: Stable. Continued home levothyroxine.

# Depression/anxiety: Stable. Continued home clonazepam. 
Continued home fluoxetine. Continued home Nortriptyline as 
above.

# GERD: Stable. Continued home pantoprazole.
